Each copy shows one minimum node cut in the accent color, with the edges it removes dashed: B, C cuts off A; C, D separates A, B from E, F; and D, E cuts off F. The card lists the three cuts." width="100%"} A node cut (or separator) is a set of nodes whose removal disconnects the graph. The smallest ones have as many nodes as the graph's node connectivity (`node_connectivity()`), and there can be many of them. `minimum_node_cut()` gives one cut between two chosen nodes; this method lists all minimum cuts of the whole graph, which shows every way the network's weakest point can be hit: the articulation points when the connectivity is 1, the pairs of nodes that split a ring, and so on. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. A complete graph has no node cuts, so the result is empty. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Every minimum node cut, as a sorted list of node IDs, in sorted order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With $k$ the node connectivity and $X$ the $k$ nodes of highest degree (Kanevsky, 1993), every minimum cut is either $X$ itself or separates some $x \in X$ from a node $v$ not adjacent to it. For each such pair, the minimum $x$-$v$ separators form a lattice: starting from the one closest to $x$ (read from the residual network of a maximum flow), moving any separator node to $x$'s side and taking the closest separator again reaches all of them, each found once. The work is a few maximum flows per cut, so the method stays fast even when the number of cuts is large. Results match NetworkX's `all_node_cuts()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A ring of six nodes falls apart when any two non-adjacent nodes are removed, so it has nine minimum node cuts of size 2: ::: {#14c5021b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ring = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) cuts = ring.all_node_cuts() len(cuts), cuts[:3] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (9, [[1, 3], [1, 4], [1, 5]]) ``` ::: ::: In two triangles that share node `C`, the shared node is the only cut: ::: {#39202d11 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} bowtie = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "C")]) ) [[bowtie.get_label_from_id(n) for n in cut] for cut in bowtie.all_node_cuts()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [['C']] ``` ::: :::
